d_sv_content.name: Radiation Therapy for Small Cell GI Lymphoma in Cats
d_sv_content.tagline: Help us learn about the use of radiation treatment in cats with GI lymphoma
d_sv_content.description:
Small cell gastrointestinal lymphoma (SCGL) is a type of cancer that affects the digestive tract of cats. It can cause long-term weight loss, vomiting, and diarrhea. The usual treatment for SCGL includes giving pills every day. Some cats do not tolerate these medicines well. This study is testing another treatment option that does not require daily pills. The treatment uses three radiation treatments. The radiation will be given slowly to help protect your cat's digestive tract. Cats may take part in this study if they have SCGL, have had signs of the disease for more than 6 weeks, and have not yet received treatment for SCGL.


We will check your cat after radiation treatment to see how well the treatment works and whether your cat has any side effects. We will also test stool (fecal) samples to learn about the bacteria in your cat's digestive tract.


The goal of this study is to find out if this radiation treatment is safe, well tolerated, and helpful for cats with SCGL. We hope this treatment will improve the quality of life for cats with this cancer.
d_sv_content.requirements: At the beginning of the study, cats will receive three daily doses of radiation for a total of 6 Gy delivered to the entire gastrointestinal tract. Owners will provide stool samples prior to radiation and at recheck appointments performed 1-week, 1-month, 3-months, and 6-months following RT. At recheck appointments, cats will undergo a physical examination to assess clinical progress following treatment. At home, owners weigh their cats on a provided scale and complete an online survey regarding their clinical progress once weekly for a month, then once monthly for 6 months following radiation therapy.
d_sv_content.responsibilities: Owners are responsible for all diagnostic and treatment-related costs beyond the incentives described above provided by the study. Additional responsibilities include:Owners must provide stool samples from their cat prior to RT and at recheck visits 1-week, 1-month, 3-months, and 6-months following RT.Owners are responsible for completing an online survey about their cat’s progress and weighing their cat on a provided cat scale once a week for a month and once a month for 6 months following RT.Owners must disclose all current medications (including supplements) and let the study team know if they change any medications including dosing during the study.Owners must make and keep all appointments for the clinical trial, including three days of radiation and recheck visits 1-week, 1-month, 3-months, and 6-months following RT.
d_sv_content.benefits: Possible benefits include improvement or resolution of symptoms of SCGL and weight gain. Side effects could be related to radiation, anesthesia, or drug complications. Gastrointestinal toxicity, including vomiting, diarrhea, decreased appetite, or other changes, could occur from radiation therapy.
d_sv_content.compensation: Once enrolled, the costs of radiation therapy, stool testing, and recheck appointments required by the study will be covered.
d_sv_content.timeCommitment: Radiation treatment will be given under anesthesia on 3 consecutive days at the start of the study; these visits will likely take most of the day or all day. Recheck visits are required 1-week, 1-month, 3-months, and 6-months following radiation; these visits will like take 1-2 hours.
